title: Clap at the cliff
hook: You clap at a cliff and time the echo. How far away is the rock face?

doesNotKnow: that an echo's delay covers the trip there and back, so the distance is half of speed × time

misconception: An echo 1 s later means the cliff is 343 m away (one sound-second).
objective: The learner can explain that an echo's delay covers the trip out and back, so the distance to the cliff is the speed of sound times the echo time, divided by two.

claims.text: The speed of sound in still air at 20 °C is about 343 m/s, from c = sqrt(γRT/M) (stage caption 'Still air, 20 °C.'; predict question 'Sound travels 343 m each second'; reveal: 'in 1 s the sound covered 343 m in total').
claims.source: c = sqrt(γRT/M) with γ = 1.4, R = 8.314 J/(mol K), T = 293.15 K, M = 0.02897 kg/mol gives 343.2 m/s. artifacts/scratch/cm-physics-r4/check.mjs (block '68 clap-at-the-cliff', 'sound 20 C'). Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, chapter on sound waves. Brief #65 claim 1.

claims.text: Sound in sea water travels about 1,500 m each second, so a sonar ping that returns after 2 s means a seabed 1,500 m deep (recall question, options and why).
claims.source: Recorded by the fact-checker (FC wj64, 2026-10-16): the recall question states a speed for sea water that no claim covers. OpenStax College Physics 2e m42256 (Speed of Sound, Frequency, and Wavelength), table: 'Sea water 1540 m/s'.
claims.note: FC wj64 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, SO-10-2 [project:wave-j], W-1490, main 0027f27+): UNRECORDED CLAIM, recorded here by the fact-checker, so left unverified. My check: arithmetic 1,500 * 2 / 2 = 1,500 m is right; OpenStax m42256 lists sea water at 1540 m/s, so 1,500 m/s is 2.6% low but a common nominal round value (real sea water varies with temperature, salinity and depth). Suggest the builder write 'about 1,500 m each second' in the recall question. Needs a second fact-checker. | FC lane-A (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, base cdee168c; I did not record this claim, FC wj64 did): VERIFIED. Recall as in meta.json: 'Sound in sea water travels 1,500 m each second', ping back after 2 s, key '1,500 m'. Arithmetic: 1,500 x 2 = 3,000 m round trip, half = 1,500 m; the other options (750 m, 3,000 m) are the halve-twice and no-halving slips. Speed: Communications Engineering 2025, 'Leveraging satellite observations and machine learning for underwater sound speed estimation' (PMC12263853, opened via PMC OAI): 'the average seawater sound speed of about 1500 m/s'; OpenStax College Physics 2e m42256 table gives 1540 m/s for one sample (FC wj64). 1,500 m/s is the standard average. Builder, non-blocking: write 'about 1,500 m each second' in the question, since real sea water varies with temperature, salinity and depth.

recall.question: A ship's sonar ping returns from the seabed after 2 s. Sound in sea water travels 1,500 m each second. How deep is the seabed?
recall.why: In 2 s the ping covers 3,000 m, down and back up. Half of that is the depth: 1,500 m.
